page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AVX-512_VNNI. Local storage is not bundled, and there are no integrated GPUs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with large-block read and write speeds placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. Software compilation with Clang and Passmark CPU physics tests also achieve top-tier results. However, single-threaded compression and static web serving throughput perform at average levels, falling into the middle 50%.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers high cost efficiency for memory-bound and compute-heavy workloads due to its dedicated core allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory architecture. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and hardware GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for direct disk-heavy databases or deep learning training. It is highly optimized for high-performance computing workloads, scientific simulations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.

The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and exceptional memory bandwidth, placing in the top 10% of benchmarks for multi-threaded decompression and large-block memory operations. It is designed for compute-intensive and memory-bound workloads such as scientific simulations, software compilation, and parallel data processing.
